📈Don’t have your ESFA export? Estimate from payroll ▾
An estimate: 0.5% of your annual pay bill above the £15,000 allowance, plus the 10% top-up. New levy payers start with an empty account that fills monthly — leave the balance blank. Confirm against your apprenticeship service account when you have it.
📊Know your levy but not your pay bill? Work it back ▾
Reverses the levy formula: pay bill = (declared levy ÷ 0.5%) + £3,000,000 (adding back the £15,000 allowance). Enter the levy you declare via PAYE (before the government’s 10% top-up). The balance seeds your account’s opening pot. An estimate — confirm against your apprenticeship service account.

📄What should the report contain? See the format ▾
For reference — nothing to fill in here. Your tracker just needs to export one row per learner with these columns (names are matched flexibly, so slight variations are fine):
ColumnMeaningRequired
learnerName or referenceyes
standardStandard title or ST referenceyes
startOn-programme start (YYYY-MM-DD)yes
planned endPlanned end / EPA gateway daterecommended
actual endCompletion / leaving date (blank if live)optional
statuson programme / gateway / achieved / withdrawn / pausedoptional
outcomeGrade — pass / merit / distinction / failoptional
progress% complete — shows live learners as on‑track / ahead / behindoptional
priceNegotiated price (else the band is used)optional
Status and outcome are what a levy export can’t give — they unlock your real achievement rate (QAR) and completion-adjusted cost. Everything stays in your browser.
Open either in Excel or Google Sheets to see the exact layout, then match your tracker’s export to it.

STEP 02Add Apprenticeship Programmes

Select a standard — funding band and EPA date are pre-filled. 80% drawn monthly; 20% released on EPA completion.

🎯Ringfence My Levy — optional: reserve part of the pot, no plan needed ▾

Set aside part of your company levy for a team or project — even one that isn’t planned yet. The calculator checks each reservation against what the pot actually holds and shows its share. Tick Apply to my projection to reserve it, so the plan below flags any overspend.

👥Age mix — optional; unlocks employer NI relief (under-25s) & the L7 age gate ▾
Under-25 apprentices carry 0% employer NIC up to £50,270 (a real saving); at Level 7, only 16–21 stay levy-funded from Jan 2026. Leave blank to skip — the plan just uses the total learner count.
Or add an apprenticeship unit — short, single-element training, levy-funded (live Apr 2026)

GIFTTransfer / Gifting Suggestion

Employers can gift up to 50% of their annual levy to charities, supply chain partners, or SMEs — covering 100% of training and assessment costs for new starts at the receiving organisation. Unspent funds expire after 24 months (pre-Aug 2026) or 12 months (from Aug 2026).

PLANThings to Consider Before You Start  — workforce impact & timing

The levy pays the training fee. Your business absorbs the time — off-the-job (OTJ) hours pull people off the floor. This estimates that overlay cost, checks it against your team's capacity, and suggests when to start around your peak seasons.

Blended cost £/hour = the average fully-loaded hourly cost of the people coming off the floor — gross salary + employer on-costs (NI, pension, etc.) ÷ working hours, averaged across the roles involved. £18/hr ≈ a ~£30k salary fully loaded. One average keeps the plan simple; to cost a single learner at their actual wage, use the wage field on the cost-per-learner card (Programmes).
Off-the-job hours per week, by level (defaults to the statutory minimum of 6 — edit up if a programme requires more)
